mlr3L0Learn

Documentation: https://mlr3l0learn.netlify.app

mlr3L0Learn adds a regression learner for best subset selection to the mlr3 framework. It wraps L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(), which fits sparse linear models with L0, L0L1 and L0L2 penalties using coordinate descent and local combinatorial search (Hazimeh and Mazumder, 2020).

Installation 

remotes::install_github("AymaneJoestar/mlr3L0Learn")

Usage

Loading the package registers the learner regr.L0Learn in the mlr3 learner dictionary.

library(mlr3)
library(mlr3L0Learn)

task <- tsk("mtcars")
learner <- lrn("regr.L0Learn", penalty = "L0", nFolds = 5L)
learner$train(task)
learner$selected_features()

prediction <- learner$predict(task)
prediction$score(msr("regr.mse"))

The penalty strength lambda (and gamma for the "L0L1" and "L0L2" penalties) is chosen by cross-validation inside L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(). The pair with the smallest cross-validated error is used for prediction.

L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit() cannot split every number of rows into every number of folds: it fails, or returns only NaN errors, when ceiling(n / nFolds) * (nFolds - 1) >= n. For example the default nFolds = 10 does not work on the 32 rows of mtcars. The learner reports this with an informative error, so pass another nFolds.

Training does not change the global random number generator state. The cross-validation folds are controlled by the seed parameter.

A benchmark against regr.featureless, regr.cv_glmnet and a tuned k-nearest neighbors learner is in the vignette:

vignette("benchmark", package = "mlr3L0Learn")
